o1.biggest_strength: It names the real ticket cause (the 2.1-day wait for the courier's first scan) and writes a 'Packed' email that pre-explains 'no updates yet', then shows the working behind every saving.
o1.biggest_mistake: It hands over single-point targets (tickets 6,762, bra returns 28.7%) as what to expect when the owner asked for a range, and it fires fit and swap prompts at leggings buyers whose 18% return rate is below average.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Carry the selection-bias caveat into a low-to-high range for each fix, and send the post-delivery fit help only to first-time bra buyers.

o2.biggest_strength: Every fix comes with an honest low-to-high range and the arithmetic, plus a delivered-bra message that actually teaches a first-time buyer how the band and cups should feel before she decides to return.
o2.biggest_mistake: It slips on rigor by adding a day-3 SMS and by calculating the swap gain on the full 18,640 returns while still claiming the quiz cuts that base, without costing the SMS or the second-return risk.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Cost the SMS into the saving, apply the quiz reduction before the swap arithmetic, and keep the copy as warm and tight as the order-confirmation subject line.

reason: Both are strong and the numbers check out, but Output 2 gives me the honest ranges I asked for and a post-delivery message that helps a first-time bra buyer get her size right instead of just nudging a swap; Output 1 is the cleaner read but sells me single-point targets and spreads effort to leggings buyers.
